title: Batching & KV Cache Counsel: Preview-Driven Applies and Immutable Change Ledger
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Goal: Provide Optimize console users with a single-pane experience that recommends batching and KV cache configuration changes, shows precise cost/latency tradeoffs in a previewable diff, and records every apply as an immutable change ledger entry that supports fast rollback and forensic audit.

Why this matters: Customers often hesitate to apply automated batching/cache suggestions because of fear of correctness regressions or unexpected latency spikes. The console must: (1) quantify per-change cost and latency delta; (2) run a deterministic dry-run (preview) across sampled traffic; (3) allow scoped rollbacks and full immutable audit trail for compliance.

Scope: UX + product requirements for recommendation cards, preview diff playback, and immutable apply ledger. This ticket covers product acceptance, success metrics and integration points for eng and design. Implementation of runtime dry-run and backend data retention is owned by ENG-89221 and ENG-91507 (dependencies).

Key user stories:
- As a platform engineer, I want to see how an optimizer recommendation changes per-token cost and P95 latency before applying it so I can decide whether to accept it.
- As a PM, I want each apply to create an immutable ledger entry that includes a snapshot of the old/new config, preview results, and author metadata so we can audit changes for security/compliance.
- As an SRE, I want the ability to perform an isolated canary apply to a traffic segment and automatically roll back if error rate increases beyond threshold.

Acceptance criteria (must pass for this ticket to be Done):
1) Recommendation card designs in Figma with the following elements: short rationale, estimated cost delta, estimated latency delta, sample query impact, confidence band, and an explicit "Run Preview" CTA.
2) Preview model: backend dry-run that executes changes against a sampled request stream (or deterministic simulator) and returns a preview diff: token counts, cost estimate, latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), and a quality signal (re-run of sample prompts with regression scoring).
3) Preview UI: side-by-side diff view with expandable examples and a compact summary. Users can toggle to see raw JSON diff for engineers.
4) Safe apply flow: requires explicit confirmation, optional canary percentage, optional approval gate for org-level policies, and displays expected rollback steps.
5) Immutable change ledger: each apply writes a ledger entry with time, author, change-id, previous config blob (hash+snapshot), new config blob, preview result summary, and commit metadata; ledger entries are immutable and queryable via Console and API.
6) Rollback UX: one-click rollback from the ledger entry that creates a revert change request and can be executed immediately or scheduled; rollback operation itself is recorded as a ledger entry.
7) Audit retention policy documented for compliance (default 90 days, enterprise option 7 years via Private deploy).
8) E2E telemetry: events emitted for preview-run, apply-start, apply-complete, rollback-start, rollback-complete with sufficient context to link to traces/dashboards.

Non-goals: implementing runtime-safe simulators for 100% production traffic fidelity (ENG will provide best-effort sampling), advanced ML-driven recommendation tuning (separate phase).

Design considerations and trade-offs:
- Preview fidelity vs. speed: higher-fidelity previews are slower and costlier. We will provide two preview flavors: Fast (approximate, <30s) and Thorough (sampling + simulation, minutes). Default CTA uses Fast with an option to run Thorough.
- Immutable ledger storage: store blobs in object store with content-addressable hashes and keep lightweight metadata in the Console DB for queries to avoid DB bloat.
- Canary vs global apply: allow percentage-based canary to reduce blast radius. Canary requires coordination with routing (ENG-91507).
- Rollback semantics: rollback should be an explicit change (not a silent reversal) and should preserve the original apply's context for postmortems.

Telemetry and success metrics:
- Adoption: % of recommendations that are previewed prior to apply (target 60% within first month).
- Safety: % of applies requiring rollback (target <3% after launch).
- Economic impact: aggregate estimated cost savings realized from applied recommendations (target $X per customer cohort over 90 days — measured separately).
- UX metrics: time-to-preview, time-to-apply, and user satisfaction (NPS in product surveys).

Engineering handoffs / integration points:
- ENG-89221 (preview execution service): API contract required: POST /preview with config delta, returns preview-id and preview-summary.
- ENG-91507 (apply service): accepts apply requests with canary parameters and returns apply-id. Must emit ledger write event to object store and metadata to Console DB.
- Security: RBAC check on apply endpoint; SSO/people-only applies for orgs with strict policies.

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Figma mockups (desktop + mobile compact) linked in attachments.
- Product acceptance doc (Confluence) describing flows and edge cases.
- Sample API contract and example preview payloads.
- QA checklist and test prompts for preview accuracy regression tests.

Open questions:
1) What is the default preview flavor? (Design suggests Fast by default.)
2) Should ledger entries be editable for metadata (tags/notes) post-apply? (Prefer not for immutability, but allow separate 'comment' objects.)
3) Enterprise retention SLA pricing impact — coordinate with Sales.
